Delivery routes and pricing

Prepared for the operations lead

Route plan, page 1

What we did and what we recommend

Over three days we rebuilt the route map, checked it against the driver logs, priced the new zones and planned the first quarter. This page is the whole of it; the rest is the evidence.

Four zones, priced for the distance

The north zone keeps its current fee because drivers already know the stops. The south zone moves to a flat fee, which is why the quote form gets shorter. Everything else in this document is built around that fee. The depot is the product where the complaint is the delay.

Route plan, page 2

Where the new schedule sits

The chart shows how many stops each driver makes per shift under the old and new plans. Reading the chart, the new plan cuts empty miles in every zone, so the fuel bill falls.

Drivers in the south zone told us in the ride-alongs that the old map sent them back across the river twice a shift, and the dispatcher confirmed that the loop added about forty minutes to every afternoon run, with the late runs landing after the stores had already closed their receiving doors for the evening and the bread going back to the depot for a second attempt the next morning at extra cost to everyone involved in the route.

Nobody can deliver faster than the courier apps, and we do not try.

Route plan, page 3
